summary: 1. Replace passive rhetorical questions with high-stakes declarative statements featuring extreme contrasts (e.g., high-tech astronaut survival vs. a single cheap plastic sheet). 2. Script hooks in conversational Romanized Hinglish instead of formal Devanagari Hindi or dry academic English. 3. Target concrete, high-tension engineering or space survival angles rather than abstract biological or carbon-cycle topics. 4. Keep titles under 55 characters in English/Hinglish with a curiosity trigger (e.g., 'Moon Bases', 'Hydroplaning') and avoid textbook-style subclauses. 5. Maintain video duration tightly between 40–44 seconds, as longer durations (>50s) fail to convert retention despite high initial watch time.
winning_hooks: High-stakes counterintuitive statements: 'Space missions mein astronauts ke liye sirf ek thin plastic sheet jaan bacha sakti hai 🤯'
Specific high-velocity danger metrics framed with immediate physical action: '250 km/h की speed से गीली runway पर plane hydroplaning से कैसे बचता है?'
avoid: Passive rhetorical questions like 'Ever thought why...' that give viewers an immediate reason to swipe away.
Abstract, school-curriculum concepts that lack human or survival stakes (e.g., 'deep ocean snow moves carbon').
Overly long, formal Devanagari titles and hooks that read like newspaper articles rather than dynamic Shorts feeds.
Low-stakes domestic observations (e.g., leftover rajma in the fridge) that fail to generate immediate urgency in the first 2 seconds.
next_experiment: Test Hook Syntax on the same engineering topic: A (Declarative shocker: 'Ye 2-millimeter ke grooves 250 km/h ke plane ko crash hone se bachaate hain') vs. B (Standard question: 'Wet runway par plane hydroplaning se kaise bachta hai?'), keeping title, visuals, and length identical at 42 seconds.
